$comment: AFLDB source-family acquisition registry (AFLDB-ISSUE-096 stage S1). Declares, per (source_key, family), the external key shape, the payload-hash exclusion list, the required/known column subset, the round vocabulary and the independence group. Keyed by STABLE SOURCE KEY only: no database-local numeric sources.id ever appears in a tracked contract. This file declares; it does not import. Family importers belong to AFLDB-ISSUE-099 (settle), AFLDB-ISSUE-100 (lineups) and AFLDB-ISSUE-095 (ladder, deliberately absent here). Evidence citations P3/P4/P5 refer to docs/acquisition/AFLDB-2026-API-ACQUISITION.md section 13, run 2026-08-28.

notes: Accessed through fitzRoy 1.8.0, the pinned AFLDB-ISSUE-093 contract version.
Registered by migration 063 rather than by data/reference/sources.json, so the tracked reference dataset does not list it. Recorded drift; reconciling the two registries is not AFLDB-ISSUE-096 work.
Same registration drift as squiggle_api.

The AFL.com.au API reached through fitzRoy fetch_lineup_afl / fetch_player_details_afl has NO sources row anywhere today. Declared here so its families carry their proven shape and independence group; registering the row belongs to the family issue that first needs provenance. Until then no family of this source may carry promotion_policy 'reviewed' - enforced by the registry validator.

afltables_2026.description: AFL Tables in-season round numbering for 2026.

squiggle_2026.description: Squiggle round numbering. Preseason / Opening Round is round 0, one lower than AFL Tables from 2024 onward.

anchors.meaning: Opening Round, 2026-03-05 (same match AFL Tables numbers 1)

kali_2026.description: Kali /matches round numbering. Opening Round is round 0. Declared as its own vocabulary even though it agreed with squiggle_2026 on every jointly observed 2026 game (P1): a per-source declaration is the contract, and agreement is evidence, not identity.

anchors.meaning: Opening Round, 2026-03-05 to 2026-03-08 (ids 11405-11409), the same games AFL Tables numbers 1
last home-and-away round, completed 2026-08-23 (AFL Tables numbers it 25)

afl_api_2026.description: AFL API round.roundNumber. Finals share the numeric home-and-away sequence, so the same integer denotes a different round than in the other two vocabularies.

anchors.meaning: Round 20 (round.name), a home-and-away round whose name matches its number
Wildcard Finals (round.name), NOT the last home-and-away round

evidence: Documented games field list, probed 2026-08-28 (docs/acquisition/AFLDB-2026-API-ACQUISITION.md section 2.2).
notes: Squiggle is the completion/latency TRIGGER for the settle pass, never the authority for a fact AFL Tables also carries, so promotion_policy is 'never' by standing decision.
`updated` is a genuine upstream mutation timestamp and is therefore the one proven source_updated_at value in this registry. It stays IN the hash: it is content, not a volatile response field.
Correction/mutability policy is undocumented, so the payload hash remains the change oracle.

evidence: P1 PASS 2026-08-28 (re-run once the key became available; previously BLOCKED). 204 matches for 2026, ids 11405-11611, 14 columns.

NOT a Squiggle proxy - five independent proofs: (a) a real VALUE disagreement on a completed match, Essendon v Port Adelaide 2026-08-23, Kali 95-105 vs Squiggle 95-104 with Squiggle complete=100; (b) `crowd` populated for 80 of 204 rows while Squiggle publishes no attendance field at all; (c) disjoint id spaces, 0 shared ids against Squiggle's 38494-38729; (d) a different venue vocabulary on 80 of 160 jointly observed games (Marvel Stadium vs Docklands, GMHBA Stadium vs Kardinia Park); (e) no goals/behinds, which Squiggle does carry.

`sourcedAt` is a stored per-record timestamp, not fetch time: two fetches 1.5s apart returned byte-identical payloads, and the five most recent rows carried five distinct values spread across 2026-08-21 to 2026-08-23.
notes: AMENDED 2026-08-28 by P1. This family previously sat in the 'squiggle' group as `assumed_derived_pending_probe` - the fail-closed default while P1 was blocked. P1 has now run and DISPROVED derivation, so Kali is its own independence group and Squiggle + Kali are TWO witnesses for matches.

RESIDUAL UNKNOWN, recorded rather than assumed away: P1 disproves PAIRWISE derivation, which is what this contract's independence definition tests. It does NOT exclude a COMMON ultimate upstream (both could read AFL.com.au). Corroboration by these two groups is therefore weaker than two fully independent witnesses, and a disagreement between them is a review signal, never an auto-resolution.

Kali's round vocabulary agreed with Squiggle's on all 160 jointly observed games and Opening Round is round 0 in both - a shared convention, not proof of a shared dataset. It is still declared as its own vocabulary (kali_2026).

`crowd` is null for 124 of 204 rows and `startDatetime` for 142 of 204: these are genuine NULLs, not zeros, and must never be read as zero attendance. AFL Tables remains the attendance authority (P5: `Attendance` 0 NA).

promotion_policy stays 'never': AFL Tables is the authority for any fact it also carries. Kali is now a genuine corroborating witness, which is ISSUE-097's to exploit - it does not make Kali promotable.

evidence: P2 PASS 2026-08-28 (re-run once the key became available; previously BLOCKED). /player-stats rows carry matchId, playerName, teamId and 17 statistics; /player-stats-advanced carries matchId, playerName, teamId and 17 more. NEITHER PROJECTS A PLAYER ID.
/players holds 2,865 players with a stable numeric `id` (2,865 distinct, 0 null) and a stable slug `onlineId` (2,865 distinct, 0 null), but 19 names are shared by 38 players.

The documented `player_id` filter WORKS against the numeric id (player_id=301 returned 17 rows, all Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera); the slug is rejected with HTTP 400. So Kali holds the player id internally on stat rows and simply does not project it.
notes: FAIL CLOSED - THE GAP, RECORDED: there is no stable provider player identifier on the player-stat grain, so a Kali stat row cannot be given a durable source identity. This family stays identity_only and may never be projected or promoted. AFL Tables profile `url` remains the sole proven player-match identity for 2026 (P5).

Name + team context is a HEURISTIC and must not be promoted to an identity. It resolved 200 of 200 sampled round-20 rows (2 ambiguous by name, 0 after applying teamId), but the population contains same-name players on the SAME team (two Alwyn Daveys, both currentTeamId 'essendon'), and `currentTeamId` is the player's CURRENT team, not the team at match time - so the heuristic degrades exactly where history matters.

The one viable identity path is enumeration: page /players (2,865 rows) and fetch /player-stats per player_id. At the free tier's 1,000 requests/day that is a multi-day crawl for one season, which is a real design constraint, not a detail.
Kali covers 19 of AFLDB's 21 player_match_stats columns, so it stays a useful statistics corroborator IF the identity gap is ever closed. Closing it is not ISSUE-096 work.

evidence: Probed 2026-08-28: the public /fixture endpoint returned Squiggle's games schema with Squiggle's own id 38494 and the identical `updated` string "2026-03-05 22:16:49" - a verbatim proxy.
notes: Recorded because a derived source is represented by an explicit derives_from edge, never by being quietly omitted: it remains a useful availability and latency signal even though it is not a second witness.
AFLDB does not consume this endpoint; it consumes /matches above.

evidence: P5 PASS 2026-08-28: 207 distinct matches for 2026, 2026-03-05 to 2026-08-23, rounds 1-25 with no finals rows yet; `Attendance` 0 NA across 9,522 player-match rows.

AFLDB-ISSUE-099 T3 (validated 2026-08-28, 48/48): tools/migration/import_fitzroy_core.py emits exactly these 18 payload columns as MATCH_PAYLOAD_COLUMNS, with periods 1-4 both sides preserved cumulative-to-date and every absent value NULL.
notes: The bundle names this family `afltables.match`; this registry keys it as (source_key `afltables`, family `match`), exactly as squiggle_api/match is keyed. The dotted form is the wire name, the pair is the contract key.

ONE observation, TWO canonical targets: `matches` and `match_period_scores`. Migration 074's ux_promotion_candidates_pending is unique on (source, family, external_record_id, target_table), so target-specific candidates are the designed dimension — not two families.

COMPOSED KEY: the two club components of external_record_id are the RESOLVED historical club identities, not the raw strings listed here. `home_team_raw`/`away_team_raw` are the payload columns the key is derived FROM; ClubResolver turns each into exactly one historical identity or fails closed, and the resulting key is byte-identical to matches.match_key.

The record is a results.csv row PLUS the match-grain supplements AFL Tables repeats on every player row (attendance, local start time, quarter scores), deduplicated at source with two distinct non-null values failing the record closed.

zero_is_missing_columns is deliberately EMPTY. `attendance` 0 is a legitimate recorded value that cites its source, and a 0 score is real; absence is NULL. Listing any column here would convert a real 0 into a NULL and is exactly the defect this family must not have.
hash_exclusions is empty: AFL Tables publishes no fetch-date or response-noise column in this payload, so every column is content and the payload hash is the whole observation.
source_updated_at_field is null and must stay null: AFL Tables publishes no upstream mutation timestamp. Fetch time, observed_from and last_seen_at are never substituted for one.
`round_number` is nullable — it is NULL for a final — so it is known but not required. `attendance`, `match_time` and `period_scores` are likewise present-but-nullable.
promotion_policy is `reviewed`, never automatic: every proposal is a promotion_candidate for a human. AFLDB-ISSUE-099 v1 writes NO canonical row at all.

evidence: P5 PASS 2026-08-28: 9,522 x 81, 2026-03-05 to 2026-08-23, 207 distinct matches, rounds 1-25 with no finals rows yet.

AFLDB-ISSUE-099 T3 (validated 2026-08-28, 48/48): import_fitzroy_core.py emits exactly these 34 payload columns as PLAYER_MATCH_PAYLOAD_COLUMNS. The 22 statistic keys are STAT_MAP's TARGET names, mapped from the source columns by explicit name — proven by re-emitting with the CSV stat columns in reverse order and getting identical values.
notes: The bundle names this family `afltables.player_match_stats`; this registry keys it as (source_key `afltables`, family `player_match_stats`).

BINDING: the in-season identity keys on profile `url` (0 NA across 9,522 rows). `ID` is 82 NA across 5 distinct urls, none of which carries an `ID` anywhere in 2026, so `ID` is an enrichment field, is carried as the nullable `afltables_id`, and must NEVER be required.

external_key is (`url`, `match_key`): the normalised profile-URL path plus the match identity, joined as `<url path>@<match_key>`. Names are never an identity key, at any grain — `first_name`, `surname` and `player_name` are display payload only.
A row whose `url` is unknown to AFLDB is `unresolved_identity` and goes to a human. A debutant can arrive with NA `Player` and NA `DOB`, which is itself an argument for reviewed promotion.
`Substitute` is NA for all 9,522 rows: the column exists and carries nothing, so it is not declared.
`Time.on.Ground` has no player_match_stats column and is deliberately not projected, so it is not declared either.
ONE observation, TWO canonical targets: `player_match_stats` and `brownlow_round_votes`. A NULL `brownlow_votes` is NA and produces NO round-vote row — never a 0, never a played/votes filler row.

zero_is_missing_columns is deliberately EMPTY. Every statistic here is NULL when not recorded and 0 when genuinely 0, including `brownlow_votes`. Listing a column would silently convert real zeroes to nulls.

hash_exclusions is empty: no column in this payload is fetch noise. The player-grain name and DOB columns stay INSIDE the hash — a source name correction is a real source change, and reconciliation classifies it as `history_only` because it moves no projected fact field, so it advances history without proposing anything.

Match-grain fields (attendance, venue, team names, match scores) are deliberately ABSENT from this payload: they belong to `afltables.match`, so a match-level correction does not appear as a correction to every one of its player rows.

AMENDED 2026-08-28 by AFLDB-ISSUE-099 T4. This family was `identity_only` / `not_yet_declared` while its shape and key were unproven; T3 proved both, so it is now `declared` with `reviewed` promotion. Reviewed means every proposal is a promotion_candidate for a human — v1 writes NO canonical row.

evidence: P3 PASS 2026-08-28: round 25 = 104 x 19, round 20 = 468 x 20 (18 teams x 26 named players). Match CD_M20260142502, team CD_T140/CD_T30, player CD_I1020621. Identity is adequate and the CD_ namespace is shared with the roster family (P4, 26 of 26 measured).

P3b PASS 2026-08-29 (AFLDB-ISSUE-100; R 4.6.1, fitzRoy 1.8.0, same environment as P3). Re-measured both rounds in full rather than by sample: r20 468 x 20, r25 104 x 19, and the single R20-only column is `lateChanges`. R25's 19 columns are a strict subset of R20's 20.

P3b types, identical for every shared column across both shapes: 2 integer (round.roundNumber, player.playerJumperNumber), 1 logical (player.captain), the remainder character. Flat tibble, no list-columns and no nested frames.

P3b NULL/blank measurement: R20 has 0 NA in every column EXCEPT lateChanges (442 NA / 26 non-NA); R25 has 0 NA in every column. 0 blank/whitespace-only strings in every character column of both rounds. lateChanges is therefore the family's only nullable field, and there is no empty-string-as-missing idiom anywhere in the payload.
P3b external-key uniqueness re-proven: sum(duplicated) on (providerId, teamId, player.playerId) is 0 in R20 and 0 in R25. Row counts reconcile exactly at 9 x 2 x 26 = 468 and 2 x 2 x 26 = 104.

P3b fixture-vs-lineup match-set equality, both directions empty in both rounds: R20 lineup 9 / fixture 9, R25 lineup 2 / fixture 2, every match returning exactly 52 rows. fetch_fixture_afl exposes providerId as a real top-level column, so the comparison joins on the same CD_M identity and needed no substitute key.
P3b player.captain: FALSE for 468/468 (R20) and 104/104 (R25) - 572 rows, 11 matches, 22 team instances, 2 rounds, with 0 TRUE and 0 NA.
P3b player.playerJumperNumber: integer, 0 NA and 0 blanks in both rounds, observed range 1-51 (R20) and 1-47 (R25). No zero, no negative and no sentinel value observed.
P3b position: the same 20 values in both rounds with 0 NA, distributed perfectly regularly as 18 distinct on-field positions once per team plus INT x5 and EMERG x3, giving 26 named players per team.
notes: STANDING DECISION: lineups are staging-only and never become canonical participation. promotion_policy is 'never' and is not negotiable by a later family issue.

known_columns_status was 'incomplete' until AFLDB-ISSUE-100's P3b enumerated the missing column. It is `lateChanges`, it is present in R20 and absent from R25 entirely, and the set is now complete at 20. The round-20 refusal this status previously caused was correct fail-closed behaviour and was resolved by measurement, never by relaxing assertProjectableColumns.

lateChanges is a CONDITIONAL, NULLABLE, TEAM-GRAIN FREE-TEXT column and is required_columns-exempt for that reason: the column itself is absent from a round in which no match carried a late change. In R20 all 26 non-NA rows belonged to ONE (match, team) - CD_M20260142007 / CD_T130, away - repeating one identical string denormalised onto every player row of that team.

BINDING on lateChanges: never parse it, never name-match it, and never infer substitution, participation or withdrawal from it. Its measured content is abbreviated human names with NO provider player ids, so joining it to player.playerId would require exactly the name matching this repository forbids at every grain. It is retained as raw observation material only; whether a separate team-grain snapshot projection is warranted is an explicit L3 decision and it must never be silently duplicated as a player fact.

PRE/POST-CHANGE STATE IS UNKNOWN, recorded rather than assumed away: in the single observed late change both the named incoming and the named outgoing player still appear in the returned player rows. Whether a match's rows reflect the team before or after a late change cannot be established from n=1, and resolving it from the EMERG or INT position values would be an inference the position vocabulary does not support.
There is NO substitute field. EMERG and INT are positions within the 20-value position vocabulary, not a medical-sub marker.
utcStartTime is the scheduled event start time and is a typed projection field. It is NOT an upstream mutation timestamp and must never populate source_updated_at.

player.captain is NOT PROJECTABLE in v1. P3b measured it FALSE for 572 of 572 rows across 11 matches and 22 team instances with 0 TRUE and 0 NA; every AFL team names a captain, so the field carries no captain signal in the source as measured. It is deliberately NOT listed in zero_is_missing_columns - that list is for a value that means missing, and the correct v1 treatment here is to project nothing at all. It stays in known_columns so that its disappearance or a change in its type remains detectable source drift.
zero_is_missing_columns is deliberately EMPTY. The only measured false/zero-like sentinel is player.captain, and it is handled by not projecting the field rather than by nulling it.
hash_exclusions is empty and stays empty: the lineup payload carries no fetch-date or response-noise column, so every column is content and the payload hash is the whole observation.

ABSENCE SWEEPING IS DISABLED for this family in v1, by decision and not by omission. P3b proved exact fixture-to-lineup MATCH-SET equality, which proves every fixture was queried; it does NOT prove that the set of player rows returned for an individual team is complete on every future run. markMissingObservationsAbsent must therefore never be called for afl_api.lineup, absent_since must never be set for it, and a missing player row must never be read as a withdrawal. Enabling absence semantics requires an explicit durable row-grain completeness contract and belongs to a future issue.
Observation persistence still reuses migration 074 unchanged: a changed payload creates a normal version and an identical payload stays idempotent. Only the absence sweep is withheld.

The observed vocabularies of status, teamStatus, teamType, compSeason.shortName and position are MEASUREMENTS, not exhaustive provider contracts, and must not become closed database or source enum CHECKs. Two rounds of one competition produced only 2, 2, 2, 1 and 20 distinct values respectively. Presence and type drift stay fail-closed through this column contract instead.

evidence: P4 PASS 2026-08-28: Carlton 2026 = 46 x 17. providerId CD_I1000953 alongside a separate numeric id 692. All 26 of 26 distinct round-20 Carlton lineup player.playerId values were found as providerId here - a measured join, not a shared-prefix inference.
P4: dateOfBirth 0 NA across 46 rows; weightInKg = 0 for 46 of 46 rows.
notes: `data_accessed` is AFLDB's own fetch date, not an upstream timestamp. It is the proven case for the hash exclusion list: without excluding it every fetch would look like a correction and idempotence would fail. It must never populate source_updated_at either.
BINDING: weightInKg = 0 is systematic zero-as-missing across every row and maps to NULL. Promoting it as a fact would write 0 kg for every player.

This source does NOT displace AFL Tables `url` as primary player identity. providerId is a SECONDARY external_identities row and routes through the AFLDB-ISSUE-092 population-drop gate. A new player remains a human decision.
promotion_policy stays 'not_yet_declared': the roster family has no successor issue and the afl_api source has no sources row, so no promotion may occur. The registry validator enforces both.
